claims.evidence: This is a result from the evolutionary model testing analysis.

claims.claim: The nearly sequentially complete gastral basket of AM 4766 is the first known in ornithischian dinosaurs.
claims.source: The nearly sequentially complete gastral basket of AM 4766 is the first known in ornithischian dinosaurs, and the tentative identification of gastralia in the holotype of the Chinese taxon T. confuciusi suggests that gastralia may have been present in all heterodontosaurids.
claims.evidence: This is a claim about the uniqueness of the specimen.

claims.claim: The tentative identification of gastralia in the holotype of Tianyulong confuciusi suggests that gastralia may have been present in all heterodontosaurids.
claims.source: The nearly sequentially complete gastral basket of AM 4766 is the first known in ornithischian dinosaurs, and the tentative identification of gastralia in the holotype of the Chinese taxon T. confuciusi suggests that gastralia may have been present in all heterodontosaurids.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference based on comparative observations.

claims.claim: Discovering gastralia in Heterodontosauridae is not surprising as this clade is consistently recovered as the earliest branching lineage of ornithischian dinosaurs.
claims.source: With gastralia being plesiomorphically ubiquitous across a range of tetrapod clades, discovering gastralia in Heterodontosauridae is not surprising as this clade is consistently recovered as the earliest branching lineage of ornithischian dinosaurs (Butler et al., 2008; Boyd, 2015).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on phylogenetic position, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Three-dimensional reconstruction of SRμCT data clearly demonstrate gastralia in close association with the distalmost point of the pubes.
claims.source: Three-dimensional reconstruction of our SRμCT data clearly demonstrate gastralia in close association with the distalmost point of the pubes, indicating that their complete retroversion (opisthopuby) was achieved with the gastralia still intimately coupled.
claims.evidence: This is a direct observation from the SRμCT data.

claims.claim: Complete pubic retroversion (opisthopuby) was achieved with the gastralia still intimately coupled.
claims.source: Three-dimensional reconstruction of our SRμCT data clearly demonstrate gastralia in close association with the distalmost point of the pubes, indicating that their complete retroversion (opisthopuby) was achieved with the gastralia still intimately coupled.
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the SRμCT data.

claims.claim: These observations contest previous hypotheses that reasoned that a divorce of the gastral basket from the pubis was a necessary prerequisite for ornithischian pubic retroversion.
claims.source: Together, these observations contest previous hypotheses that reasoned that a divorce of the gastral basket from the pubis was a necessary prerequisite for ornithischian pubic retroversion (Rasskin-Gutman and Buscalioni, 2001).
claims.evidence: This is an inference that contradicts a previous hypothesis, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The association of the gastralia with the distal end of the pubic rod indicates that the latter structure is homologous to the pubic shaft/apron of other archosaurs.
claims.source: Furthermore, the association of the gastralia with the distal end of the pubic rod indicates that the latter structure is homologous to the pubic shaft/apron of other archosaurs (Galton, 1970, contra references therein), and that the APP is a de novo feature.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about homology, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The APP is a de novo feature.
claims.source: Furthermore, the association of the gastralia with the distal end of the pubic rod indicates that the latter structure is homologous to the pubic shaft/apron of other archosaurs (Galton, 1970, contra references therein), and that the APP is a de novo feature.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the evolutionary origin of the APP.

claims.claim: The presence of sternal ribs in H. tucki extends the occurrence of these bones from late diverging taxa to the basalmost members of Ornithischia.
claims.source: The presence of sternal ribs in H. tucki extends the occurrence of these bones from late diverging taxa like T. neglectus and other relatively late-branching, small-bodied Late Jurassic and Cretaceous neornithischians (Carpenter and Galton, 2018; Butler and Galton, 2008) to the basalmost members of Ornithischia.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the phylogenetic distribution of sternal ribs, supported by citations.

claims.claim: This broader distribution strongly implies that the presence of sternal ribs may optimize as an ornithischian plesiomorphy.
claims.source: This broader distribution strongly implies that the presence of sternal ribs may optimize as an ornithischian plesiomorphy.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference about character evolution.

claims.claim: The sternal ribs described in H. tucki are autapomorphic in morphology, differing markedly from those of other ornithischians.
claims.source: However, the sternal ribs we describe in H. tucki are autapomorphic in morphology, differing markedly from those of other ornithischians, and showing clear evidence of being mobile about their dorsal rib and sternal plate joints (Figure 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation, supported by Figure 4.

claims.claim: The sternal ribs of H. tucki show clear evidence of being mobile about their dorsal rib and sternal plate joints.
claims.source: However, the sternal ribs we describe in H. tucki are autapomorphic in morphology, differing markedly from those of other ornithischians, and showing clear evidence of being mobile about their dorsal rib and sternal plate joints (Figure 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is an inference from the anatomy, supported by Figure 4.

claims.claim: The dorsoventrally expanded dorsal and ventral margins of the sternal ribs were likely attachment sites for intercostal musculature.
claims.source: The dorsoventrally expanded dorsal and ventral margins of these ribs were likely attachment sites for intercostal musculature and in this way perhaps analogous to similar projections (sternocostapophyses) on the sternal ribs of pterosaurs (Claessens et al., 2009), the uncinate processes of maniraptorans (Tickle et al., 2012; Codd et al., 2008), and the remarkably similar sternal ribs of the ornithothoracine J. prima (Zheng et al., 2020) – all of which are adaptations hypothesized to increase lever-arm potential and facilitate efficient deformation of the body wall to drive ventilation.
claims.evidence: This is a functional inference supported by comparative anatomy and citations.

claims.claim: The complex sternal plates of AM 4766 bear similarities with early- and late-diverging theropods such as Tawa hallae and various avialans.
claims.source: The complex sternal plates of AM 4766 are distinct from the comparatively simple 'hatchet-shaped' sternal plates of iguanodontians and the 'kidney-shaped' (reniform) sterna of other neornithischians but are not unique among Dinosauria. Instead, the complex sternal plates of AM 4766 bear similarities with early- and late-diverging theropods such as Tawa hallae (Bradley et al., 2019) and various avialans (Zheng et al., 2012; O'Connor et al., 2015), respectively.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation supported by citations.

claims.claim: Features like the tongue-shaped process of AM 4766 and the coracoid facet of Tawa hallae are strikingly similar in their dimensions, location, and abrupt change in orientation relative to the posterior half of their respective sternal plates.
claims.source: Features like the tongue-shaped process of AM 4766 and the coracoid facet of T. hallae are strikingly similar in their dimensions, location, and abrupt change in orientation relative to the posterior half of their respective sternal plates.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative observation.

claims.claim: It is unclear whether these sternal similarities are homologous, but they are likely functionally analogous.
claims.source: It is unclear whether these sternal similarities are homologous, but they are likely functionally analogous.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative statement about homology and function.

claims.claim: The nature of change in the relative length of the APP is conspicuous from both qualitative and quantitative analyses of pelvic evolution.
claims.source: The nature of change in the relative length of the APP is conspicuous from both qualitative and quantitative analyses of pelvic evolution.
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement about the results.

claims.claim: Innovation in APP length occurred early in ornithischian evolution, before the diversification of genasaurians.
claims.source: Innovation in APP length occurred early in ornithischian evolution, before the diversification of genasaurians, and after this significant early burst (see Figure 7, Table 1), modifications of the APP were generally restricted to gross shape differences that do not affect the relative length: derived ornithopods evolved a large, lobate APP with derived neoceratopsians evolving an APP that fanned-out anteriorly.
claims.evidence: This is a result from the quantitative analysis, supported by Figure 7 and Table 1.

claims.claim: After the significant early burst in APP length, modifications of the APP were generally restricted to gross shape differences that do not affect the relative length.
claims.source: Innovation in APP length occurred early in ornithischian evolution, before the diversification of genasaurians, and after this significant early burst (see Figure 7, Table 1), modifications of the APP were generally restricted to gross shape differences that do not affect the relative length: derived ornithopods evolved a large, lobate APP with derived neoceratopsians evolving an APP that fanned-out anteriorly.
claims.evidence: This is a result from the quantitative analysis, supported by Figure 7 and Table 1.

claims.claim: These results are interpreted as rapid switching of optimal phenotypes for APP size; from the plesiomorphically small condition in H. tucki to a proportionally long APP that is then maintained across all later-branching ornithischian lineages.
claims.source: We interpret these results as rapid switching of optimal phenotypes for APP size; from the plesiomorphically small condition in H. tucki to a proportionally long APP that is then maintained across all later-branching ornithischian lineages.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the quantitative results.

claims.claim: The APP was involved in a major macroevolutionary shift in ornithischian dinosaurs, which occurred immediately prior to their radiation in the Jurassic.
claims.source: We consider this as evidence that the APP was involved in a major macroevolutionary shift in ornithischian dinosaurs, which occurred immediately prior to their radiation in the Jurassic.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretive claim based on the quantitative results.

claims.claim: The timing of change in the relative length of the APP cooccurs with the reduction and loss of the gastralia and possibly the loss or reduction of sternocostal mobility.
claims.source: Moreover, the timing of this change in the relative length of the APP cooccurs with the reduction and loss of the gastralia and possibly the loss or reduction of sternocostal mobility.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the timing of evolutionary changes.

claims.claim: These results are consistent with, but greatly expand upon, Brett-Surman's hypothesis that the enlarged APP is an adaptation of ornithischians involved in driving considerable changes in abdominothoracic volume.
claims.source: These results are consistent with, but greatly expand upon, Brett-Surman's hypothesis (Brett-Surman, 1989) that the enlarged APP is an adaptation of ornithischians involved in driving considerable changes in abdominothoracic volume.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretive claim that relates the results to a previous hypothesis, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Despite highly derived pubic rod morphologies, including near loss in late branching ankylosaur taxa like Euoplocephalus tutus, the APP is retained as a process fused to the ventral surface of the ilium.
claims.source: Nevertheless, we observe that despite highly derived pubic rod morphologies, including near loss in late branching taxa like Euoplocephalus tutus, the APP is retained as a process fused to the ventral surface of the ilium (Carpenter et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is an observation about ankylosaurs, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The retention of the APP in ankylosaurs strongly implies that the APP was subject to a constraint that favoured its retention when the rest of the pubis was made redundant.
claims.source: This strongly implies that the APP was subject to a constraint that favoured its retention when the rest of the pubis was made redundant.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary constraint.

claims.claim: The pattern of pubic evolution is best explained by a 'Drift' evolutionary hypothesis and suggests a trend away from elongate pubes.
claims.source: This pattern of pubic evolution is best explained by a 'Drift' evolutionary hypothesis and suggests a trend away from elongate pubes.
claims.evidence: This is an interpretation of the quantitative results.

claims.claim: The reduction of the pubic rod is pervasive in ornithischians as it is independently lost in derived iguanodontians, neoceratopsians, and pachycephalosaurs.
claims.source: The reduction of the pubic rod is pervasive in ornithischians as it is independently lost in derived iguanodontians, neoceratopsians, and pachycephalosaurs (as well as ankylosaurs; Carpenter et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is an observation about the phylogenetic distribution of pubic rod reduction, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The reduction of the pubic rod likely signifies a relaxing of a plesiomorphic constraint between the hypaxial abdominal musculature and the pubis.
claims.source: This likely signifies a relaxing of a plesiomorphic constraint between the hypaxial abdominal musculature and the pubis.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about evolutionary constraint.

claims.claim: The reduction of the pubic rod is decoupled temporally and phylogenetically from the loss of gastralia and the expansion of the APP, strongly suggesting that the pubic rod was rendered vestigial.
claims.source: This reduction of the pubic rod is decoupled temporally and phylogenetically from the loss of gastralia and the expansion of the APP, strongly suggesting that the pubic rod was rendered vestigial.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about the functional significance of the pubic rod.

claims.claim: It is possible that modifications like the bowed ischium of neoceratopsians and the 'ischial boot' of some hadrosaurs are responses to the ischium subsuming the myological role previously played by the pubis.
claims.source: It is possible that modifications like the bowed ischium of neoceratopsians and the 'ischial boot' of some hadrosaurs are responses to the ischium subsuming the myological role previously played by the pubis.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference about functional morphology.

claims.claim: The changing vertebrocostal orientations along the axial column of H. tucki support the bipartite and dorsally immobile lung previously reconstructed in ornithischians and silesaurids.
claims.source: The changing vertebrocostal orientations along the axial column of H. tucki observed here (Figure 6) support the bipartite and dorsally immobile lung previously reconstructed in ornithischians and silesaurids (Schachner et al., 2011; Brocklehurst et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on anatomical observations, supported by Figure 6 and citations.

claims.claim: The proposed ventilatory mechanism for Ornithischia was likely functionally distinct from the hepatic piston model present in crocodilians, although the two may have been anatomically convergent.
claims.source: Considering that a dorsally immobilized, anatomically and functionally heterogeneous lung has been reconstructed for all of Ornithischia (Schachner et al., 2011; Brocklehurst et al., 2018), and that the M. diaphragmaticus of extant crocodilians is coupled with a flexible lung and shifting viscera, the proposed ventilatory mechanism for Ornithischia was likely functionally distinct from the hepatic piston model present in crocodilians, although the two may have been anatomically convergent.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference about functional morphology, supported by citations.

claims.claim: The anatomical features presented provide consilient evidence that H. tucki preserves morphologies that reflect early steps in the evolution of a novel means of lung ventilation in ornithischian dinosaurs.
claims.source: The anatomical features presented here provide consilient evidence that H. tucki preserves morphologies that reflect early steps in the evolution of a novel means of lung ventilation in ornithischian dinosaurs.
claims.evidence: This is a summary interpretive claim.

claims.claim: Gastralia are widespread among Palaeozoic and Mesozoic tetrapods but have never before been unambiguously reported in Ornithischia.
claims.source: Gastralia are widespread among Palaeozoic and Mesozoic tetrapods but have never before been unambiguously reported in Ornithischia.
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the distribution of gastralia, based on established knowledge.

claims.claim: Among other dinosaurian lineages, theropods retain their gastral basket until the evolution of neornithine birds.
claims.source: Among other dinosaurian lineages, theropods retain their gastral basket until the evolution of neornithine birds, and sauropodomorphs lose their gastralia relatively late in their evolutionary history at the base of Eusauropoda – potentially retaining gastralia even during the emergence of Neosauropoda (Tschopp and Mateus, 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the phylogenetic distribution of gastralia, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: Sauropodomorphs lose their gastralia relatively late in their evolutionary history at the base of Eusauropoda.
claims.source: Among other dinosaurian lineages, theropods retain their gastral basket until the evolution of neornithine birds, and sauropodomorphs lose their gastralia relatively late in their evolutionary history at the base of Eusauropoda – potentially retaining gastralia even during the emergence of Neosauropoda (Tschopp and Mateus, 2013).
claims.evidence: This is a statement about the phylogenetic distribution of gastralia, supported by a citation.

claims.claim: The reduction or loss of the gastralia independently occurs in other major tetrapod lineages like stem turtles and eutheriodont therapsids including mammals.
claims.source: The reduction or loss of the gastralia independently occurs in other major tetrapod lineages like stem turtles (Lyson et al., 2013; Schoch and Sues, 2020), and eutheriodont therapsids including mammals (Cisneros et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is a comparative statement supported by citations.

claims.claim: Specialized lung ventilatory mechanisms are present in all extant clades that have lost (birds, mammals) or co-opted the gastralia (turtles).
claims.source: Interestingly, specialized lung ventilatory mechanisms are present in all extant clades that have lost (birds, mammals) or co-opted the gastralia (turtles).
claims.evidence: This is a comparative statement based on knowledge of extant taxa.

claims.claim: Some workers have explicitly linked the loss of gastralia and subsequent thoracic and lumbar differentiation of therocephalian and cynodont therapsid axial skeletons to the evolution of a mammalian-style, diaphragm-driven ventilatory arrangement.
claims.source: Some workers have explicitly linked the loss of gastralia and subsequent thoracic and lumbar differentiation of therocephalian and cynodont therapsid axial skeletons to the evolution of a mammalian-style, diaphragm-driven ventilatory arrangement (Perry et al., 2010; Brink, 1956).

results.result: A new, fully articulated specimen of Heterodontosaurus tucki (AM 4766) reveals novel postcranial features including a large anteriorly projecting sternum, paddle-shaped sternal ribs, and the first complete gastral basket recovered in Ornithischia.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C7 and C43-C47 describe the specimen and its novel anatomical features, supported by synchrotron imaging data (C4) and detailed anatomical descriptions with accompanying figures. The claim that this is the first gastral basket in Ornithischia (C7, C90) is supported by direct observation and comparative analysis (C47, C123). The anatomical descriptions are consistent across multiple claims and supported by imaging evidence.

results.result: The sternal plates of AM 4766 are complex, sub-rectangular structures with an autapomorphic tongue-shaped anteromedial process and bear similarities to early-diverging theropods such as Tawa hallae and various avialans.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C56 provide detailed anatomical descriptions of the sternal plates supported by Figure 2 and comparisons with other specimens (SAM-PK-K1332). Claims C103-C105 establish comparative similarities with theropods, though the homology versus functional analogy remains uncertain (C105). The anatomical observations are well-documented, though functional interpretations are speculative.

results.result: Three pairs of spatulate sternal ribs with monocondylar articulations are preserved in AM 4766, showing clear evidence of mobility and differing markedly from other ornithischians but resembling pterosaurs and the avialan Jeholornis prima.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C62 describe the sternal rib morphology with support from Figures 3 and 4 and comparative citations. Claims C98-C102 establish the phylogenetic significance and functional interpretations. The anatomical observations are well-supported by imaging data, though functional inferences about muscle attachment (C102) are speculative but reasonably grounded in comparative anatomy.

results.result: AM 4766 preserves paired clavicles and an ossified suprascapula, features with sporadic distribution in Ornithischia, with the clavicles being proportionally longer than those of ceratopsians.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C71 describe the clavicles and suprascapula with support from Figure 5 and comparative citations (C65, C70, C71). The anatomical descriptions are detailed and supported by imaging data. The comparative measurements (C67) provide quantitative support. However, uncertainty remains about whether the suprascapula is ossified or cartilaginous, which the authors acknowledge.

results.result: Synchrotron scanning reveals that the parapophyses migrate anterodorsally along the vertebral column, and the entire internal structure of the vertebral column lacks pneumatic chambers or fossae, conclusively showing that early ornithischians lacked postcranial skeletal pneumaticity (PSP).
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C74 are supported by SRμCT data and Figure 6, providing direct observational evidence of vertebral morphology and the absence of PSP. Claim C120 connects these observations to previous reconstructions of bipartite lungs with supporting citations. The use of high-resolution imaging provides strong evidence for the absence of PSP, addressing a key question in ornithischian respiratory evolution.

results.result: Quantitative phylogenetic analysis reveals that the anterior pubic process (APP) underwent rapid elongation early in ornithischian evolution at the base of Genasauria, best explained by an 'Early Burst' model, with declining rates of change in later-branching lineages and no reversions to the plesiomorphic condition.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C89 present the quantitative analysis results with strong statistical support (r² > 0.96 for APP, AICc weight 99.99%, p<0.01 for Early Burst model). Claims C106-C111 provide interpretations of these results. The analysis is methodologically sound with appropriate phylogenetic corrections (pGLS), though the choice of femoral length as a body size proxy has acknowledged limitations for stegosaurs. The statistical evidence strongly supports the Early Burst model for APP evolution.

results.result: Three-dimensional reconstruction of SRμCT data demonstrates that complete pubic retroversion (opisthopuby) was achieved with gastralia still intimately coupled to the distal pubes, contesting previous hypotheses and indicating that the pubic rod is homologous to the pubic shaft of other archosaurs while the APP is a de novo feature.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C97 are supported by direct observation from SRμCT data showing the spatial relationship between gastralia and pubes. The inference about homology (C96, C97) is supported by this anatomical association and a citation (Galton, 1970). This finding directly contradicts a previous hypothesis (C95, citing Rasskin-Gutman and Buscalioni, 2001), providing new evidence about the evolution of the ornithischian pelvis.

results.result: Tentative identification of gastralia in Tianyulong confuciusi suggests that gastralia may have been present in all heterodontosaurids, which is unsurprising given the basal phylogenetic position of Heterodontosauridae.
results.evaluation: Claim C49 explicitly states the identification is 'tentative' based on similarity with AM 4766. Claim C91 is speculative (evidence_type includes SPECULATION), and C48 notes that fragments in SAM-PK-K1332 'could potentially represent displaced ossified tendons or posteriormost dorsal ribs.' The inference about all heterodontosaurids (C91) is based on limited evidence from only two specimens, one of which is tentatively identified. More specimens are needed to support this broader claim.

results.result: The evolution of APP length is consistent with Brett-Surman's hypothesis of a ventilatory function, with evidence that APP changes are divorced from locomotory influences based on phylogenetic timing, allometry of the ambiens muscle, and anatomical position relative to the ribcage.
results.evaluation: Claims C112 and C138-C141 present multiple lines of evidence against a locomotory function: phylogenetic timing divorced from quadrupedality (C138), negative allometry of ambiens muscle in extant taxa (C139), and anatomical constraints (C140). Claims C113-C119 discuss pubic rod reduction and evolutionary constraints. The evidence is well-reasoned and supported by citations, though some inferences about evolutionary constraints (C114, C117) are speculative. The case against locomotory function is stronger than the positive case for ventilatory function.

results.result: H. tucki is interpreted as a transitional taxon preserving early steps in the evolution of a novel 'pelvic bellows' ventilation mechanism in ornithischian dinosaurs, with the small APP serving as a nascent attachment for a hypothesized 'puboperitoneal muscle' analogous to the dorsal component of M. diaphragmaticus in crocodilians.
results.evaluation: Claims C142-C153 present a detailed evolutionary model, but much of this is speculative inference (evidence_type includes SPECULATION for C148, C149, C151, C152, C153). The model is internally consistent and integrates the anatomical observations, but key elements like the existence and function of the 'puboperitoneal muscle' (C148, C149) are hypothetical. Claims C169-C170 assert broader significance, but these depend on the speculative ventilatory model. While the anatomical observations are solid, the functional and evolutionary interpretations require additional evidence such as muscle attachment site analysis or biomechanical modeling.

results.result: The proposed ornithischian ventilatory mechanism was likely functionally distinct from the crocodilian hepatic piston, though possibly anatomically convergent, with phylogenetic bracketing predicting intrapulmonary unidirectional airflow compatible with the model.
results.evaluation: Claim C121 is explicitly speculative (evidence_type includes SPECULATION) about functional distinctness from crocodilians. Claim C144 about unidirectional airflow is based on phylogenetic bracketing with supporting citations, which is reasonable but indirect. Claim C145 about Silesaurus provides suggestive evidence but is based on a single taxon with controversial phylogenetic relationships. The functional distinctness claim requires biomechanical analysis or additional comparative evidence to be well-supported.

results.result: Gastralia are widespread among Paleozoic and Mesozoic tetrapods but were previously unknown in Ornithischia, with their reduction or loss occurring independently in multiple tetrapod lineages that evolved specialized ventilatory mechanisms, and playing important roles in ventilation in non-avian theropods through 'cuirassal breathing.'
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C132 provide context about gastralial distribution and function across tetrapods, supported by multiple citations to previous research. These are well-established facts from the literature (evidence_type includes CITATION and KNOWLEDGE). The comparative framework is important for interpreting the significance of gastralia in AM 4766, though these claims are primarily literature review rather than new findings.

results.result: Investigation into dinosaur respiration has historically focused narrowly on postcranial skeletal pneumaticity (PSP), but recent research shows that respiratory systems are more complex and variable, suggesting that archosaurs demonstrate remarkably labile respiratory evolution and that the evolution of the APP may be linked to ornithischian diversification.
results.evaluation: Claims C154-C158 are supported by citations to previous research and represent a fair assessment of the literature and recent developments. Claims C159-C162 are more speculative (evidence_type includes SPECULATION for C160-C162) about broader implications. The critique of PSP-focused approaches is well-founded given the evidence presented in the manuscript, though the claims about the link between APP evolution and diversification (C162) are speculative and would require additional macroevolutionary analysis.

results.result: Ornithischian respiratory mechanisms remain poorly understood, with ornithischians lacking key ventilatory structures present in other diapsids (gastralia, mobile sternal ribs, PSP) and having a uniquely bipartite lung structure, strongly suggesting a fundamentally different lung structure from other ornithodirans despite occupying similar ecological niches.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C40 establish the context and knowledge gaps that motivate the study. These are supported by citations to previous research (evidence_type includes CITATION) and represent established knowledge in the field. However, claims C27-C28 about ornithischians lacking gastralia and mobile sternal ribs are challenged by the new specimen AM 4766, which is a key finding of the paper. The characterization of the knowledge gap is accurate for the pre-AM 4766 state of knowledge.

results.result: In archosaurian ventilation models, pelvic involvement is ubiquitous with anterior bony projections of the pubic region being key components, and previous authors have highlighted the APP as integral for interpreting ornithischian lung ventilation, though its role has been contentious with alternative locomotory functions proposed.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C137 summarize previous research on archosaurian ventilation and the APP, supported by citations (evidence_type includes CITATION). These establish the theoretical framework for interpreting the new findings. The summary of previous hypotheses is accurate and provides important context, though these are not new findings from the current study.

results.result: Specimen AM 4766 was recovered from the upper Elliot Formation in strata correlating with the Massospondylus Assemblage Zone, likely Sinemurian in age, from a light red, clast-rich, very fine-grained sandstone consistent with a seasonally wet, fluvio-lacustrine system.
results.evaluation: Claims C163-C165 provide geological context supported by citations (Viglietti et al., 2020; Bordy et al., 2020; Bordy et al., 2004a). The stratigraphic and sedimentological information is important for contextualizing the specimen but is straightforward descriptive information rather than a novel finding. The age determination is qualified as 'likely' (C164), appropriately reflecting uncertainty.

results.result: Ornithischian dinosaurs were ecologically prominent Mesozoic herbivores with a highly derived body plan, and Heterodontosaurus tucki has long been recognized as crucial for resolving early ornithischian phylogenetic relationships, though most studies have examined a single specimen (SAM-PK-K1332).
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C2 and C11-C16 establish general background about ornithischians, supported by established knowledge and citations. Claims C41-C42 establish the importance of H. tucki and the limitation of previous studies to a single specimen, supported by citations. These are accurate statements that provide context but are not novel findings. They establish the rationale for studying the new specimen AM 4766.
